audits.body:
Materializing flowshot-git from local mirror...
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/flowshot-git.git...
Cloned flowshot-git
Analyzing flowshot-git AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
`makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources and evaluates the PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope. In this file, that scope contains exclusively standard, declarative AUR metadata: pkgname, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends/makedepends/optdepends/checkdepends arrays, provides, conflicts, source, b2sums (SKIP, which is standard for VCS sources and not a failure criterion), and options.

There is no executable code at the top level: no command substitutions that download or run payloads, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, no obfuscation or encoding tricks, and no network activity. The `source` entry (`$_pkgname::git+$url.git`) merely declares that the package will be fetched from the project's own upstream GitHub repository — a normal VCS declaration, not an executable action.

The functions `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` contain git/cargo operations and install commands, but these are inside function definitions and are never executed by `--printsrcinfo`; they are out of scope for this gate and will be audited in the full PKGBUILD review. The `pkgver()` function's git commands reference the declared upstream URL and use no remote override, so even a future full audit would show no indication of pulling from an unrelated host.

No security issues are present in the portion of the file that this command executes.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard declarative PKGBUILD, no executable global code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Standard declarative PKGBUILD, no executable global code.

All dependencies and optdepends are standard library/tool dependencies for a Wayland/Qt application. The package version format 0.1.0.r0.g0000000 is a normal git describe output. There is no evidence of injected malicious code, data exfiltration, backdoors, or execution of attacker-controlled code.
